title: Exoplanets: Detection Methods
meta_desc: A-Level Astronomy: transit photometry, radial velocity and Kepler.

walkthroughs.body_html: A planet passing in front of its star causes a tiny dip in brightness (Earth transiting the Sun would dip 0.01%). Kepler (2009-2018) and TESS use this method.
A planet tugs its host star into a small orbit. The star's Doppler shift reveals the planet — the method that found the first hot Jupiter, 51 Pegasi b, in 1995.
Direct imaging works for young, hot, far-out giants. Microlensing uses a foreground star's gravity to magnify a background star — a one-off chance event but sensitive to distant planets.

options: By picking up the planet's radio signals.
It measures the planet's surface temperature.
By directly photographing the planet's surface.

The region inside the star itself.

options: The region inside the star itself.
